newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - August 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - August 19.

text.p: Prepared by The Broadcast Monitoring Company for Reuters
FINANCIAL TIMES
BT, MCI EXPECTED TO STICK TO DEAL TERMS

Securities lawyers at the Securities and Exchange Commission in New York have indicated the proposed merger between British Telecom and MCI will go ahead with no alterations aside from a slight modification of strategy at MCI aimed at appeasing BT shareholders. BT's shares-and-cash offer valued MCI at $28.67 billion on Monday (17.76 billion pounds), and the merger is expected to receive approval from the U.S. Federal Communications Commission later this week.
RJB BLAMED GEOLOGY FOR ASFORDBY CLOSURE

Due to what it labelled geological difficulties and problems in maintaining safe and economic mining conditions, RJB mining has closed the Ashfordby colliery in Leicester, eliminating up to 500 jobs. About 360 million pounds has been invested in the mine, which opened in 1977 and had yet to record a profit, and in 1996 accounted for only 700,000 of the 37 million tonnes of coal produced by RJB, Britain's biggest coal miner.
JAGUAR PLANS NEW SMALL CAR TO BOOST PRODUCTION

Jaguar, the UK luxury car subsidiary of Ford, is to begin the development of a new car said to hold 'significant commercial potential' which will likely lift production at the company its present 50,000 level to 200,000 per year. The BMW 3 series-sized car is in development at the group's Whitley engineering centre, codenamed X400, and is currently undergoing a 90-day feasibility study. Though it seems likely the car will become commercially available before long, it has not yet been determined whe re it will be manufactured.
EUROPEAN GROUPS WIN CHINA DAM CONTRACTS

The Chinese government has awarded contracts to supply power for the country's Three Gorges dam to two consortia, one led by Anglo-French group GEC-Alsthom and one led by Siemens. GEC-Alsthom's group won the majority of the 490.7 million pound order, and is to supply eight power units for the first stage of the $30 billion project, while the group led by Siemens will supply the remaining six generators and turbines. The 600-km-long Three Gorges project will displace one million people and will be completed by 2009.
GERMAN MINISTER SAYS HIGH JOBLESS RATE WILL CONTINUE

Gunter Rexrodt, the German economics minister, has stated that despite the country's rapid economic growth rate, 1998 figures will probably show only a 'slight' decline in joblessness, with the biggest reductions in unemployment coming in the west. High wages and overcapacity in the building industry have been blamed for lack of jobs in the east. Despite unemployment raising government spending and lowering tax revenues, Rexrodt stressed Maastricht criteria for European monetary union could still be met - though he would not guarantee Germany would meet the three per cent of budget deficit EMU target.
BP TO SUE GREENPEACE FOR 1.4M STG

British Petroleum has announced it will sue Greenpeace UK for 1.4 million pounds stemming from the occupation of its Stena Dee mobile oil rig in the North Atlantic last week by four environmental protesters. BP claims the disruption prevented it from adhering to its exploration schedule and served to increase the 100,000 pound-per-day bill for the rig's rental. Greenpeace UK, despite having recorded an income of 6.8 million pounds in 1996, said that if BP won the lawsuit, it may be forced to go o ut of business.
CIRCUIT BOARD MAKERS FACE RISE IN LEGAL CLAIMS

Following an increase in the number of legal claims from customers claiming defective printed circuit board products, the Printed Circuit Interconnection Federation has unveiled a special insurance package for its members. Swiss-based Zurich Insurance is offering the package, which is aimed at protecting manufacturers against 'consequential losses' resulting from faulty products. Brian Haken, director of the federation, said almost half of the group's 140 members had been hit by damage claims of up to 1 0,000 pounds.
ARGOS INTERIM PROFITS DOWN BUT WINDFALLS BOOST SALES

Argos, the high street retailer, has reported a 12 percent fall in interim pre-tax profits to 28.1 million pounds on sales of 627 million pounds due to what chief executive Mike Smith labelled a strong first half in 1996 combined with higher costs and patchy consumer demand. Smith noted, however, that the company had experienced a recent uplift in second-half sales because of the impact of building society windfalls, though he warned the present 'buoyancy in consumer confidence and overall retail sales may not be sustainable'.
CORTECS FLU DRUG WINS US PATENT

Anglo-Australian biotech concern Cortecs International has been awarded a US patent for its oral influenza vaccine, Flustat. Cortecs announced it had received approval from the Western Australian supreme court for its UK plc status, which should be completed in September accompanied by a primary listing in London and secondary listings in Australia and the U.S.
BURMAH CASTROL CONTINUES REVAMP OF CHEMICALS SIDE

UK oil concern Burmah Castrol will further the reorganisation of its chemicals division with the sale of Columbia Cement and the 23 million-pound purchase of the SMC Group, which produces coatings and resins. Burmah declared the acquisition of SMC would raise its profile in the European market for binders and coatings used to make foundry mouldings, and will be merged with Burmah's existing foundry division.
